question_text: According to the course material, a fallacy is not necessarily an invalid argument; rather it is:
option_a: an argument that appears sufficiently acceptable, but which contains errors
option_d: a definition by genus and difference
explanation: Fallacious argument or reasoning is not necessarily an invalid argument. Rather it is an argument that appears sufficiently acceptable, but which contains errors (Oke and Audu, 2006:107).

question_text: According to the course material, a fallacy is usually committed in the process of:
option_a: moving from the premises of an argument to its conclusion
explanation: Usually, a fallacy is committed in the process of moving from the premises of an argument to its conclusion.

question_text: According to the course material, major formal fallacies you should know include Affirming the Consequent, Denying the Antecedent, Fallacy of Four Terms, Existential Fallacy and:
option_a: Fallacy of Exclusive Premises
explanation: Know major Formal fallacies such as Affirming the Consequent, Denying the Antecedent, Fallacy of Four Terms, Existential Fallacy and Fallacy of Exclusive Premises.

question_text: According to the course material, the fallacy of complex or loaded question is committed when:
option_a: two or more questions are asked together at once and an answer to one allows a conclusion regarding the other
option_b: a valid modus ponens is used
explanation: This fallacy of complex question is committed when two or more questions are asked together at once and as an answer to one question allows one to draw a conclusion regarding the other question.

question_text: According to the course material, Have you stopped beating your wife? is an example of:
option_a: fallacy of complex or loaded question
explanation: Example of such fallacy: Have you stopped beating your wife? The questioner assumes the person addressed has a wife, and beats his wife.

question_text: According to the course material, the fallacy of leading question occurs when an arguer attempts to base his claim on a:
option_a: prepared answer, such as a witness under cross examination
explanation: This occurs when an arguer attempts to base his claim on a prepared answer, such as a witness under cross examination.

question_text: According to the course material, the leading-question fallacy is commonly used by:
option_a: Lawyers and any other investigative officers to extract information from suspects and criminals
explanation: This fallacy is commonly used by Lawyers and any other investigative officers to extract information from suspects and criminals.

question_text: According to the course material, begging the question is also called:
option_a: petitio principii
explanation: Fallacy of Begging the question (Petitio-principii).

question_text: According to the course material, fallacies of presumption are committed when there is the assumption in the argument's premises of:
option_a: what the arguer is out to prove
explanation: This fallacy is committed, when there is the assumption in the argument's premises, of what the arguer is out to prove.

question_text: According to the course material, Unit 2 of Module 4 particularly discusses fallacies involving:
option_a: weak induction and fallacies of presumption
explanation: Here, we will particularly be discussing the fallacies involving weak induction and fallacies of presumption.

question_text: According to the course material, a definition is a sine qua non tool for:
option_a: effective communication
explanation: A definition is a sine qua non tool for effective communication. We cannot avoid vagueness, ambiguity or equivocation unless we rightly define our words or terms.

question_text: According to Stebbing, cited in the course material, a definition consists of the word to be defined, the definiendum, and:
option_a: the expression which defines it, the definiens, which must contain more than one word
explanation: It consists of the word to be defined, that is, the definiendum (which may be a single word) and the expression which defines the expression that is, the definiens (which must contain more than one word) (Stebbing:1993).

question_text: According to the course material, the classical description of definition as a statement of essence of a thing has its origin in:
option_a: Aristotle's assertion that an object's essential attribute forms its essential nature
explanation: This description was given by the classical thought and it has its origin in Aristotle's assertion that an object's essential attribute forms its essential nature.

question_text: According to the course material, philosophers distinguish between:
option_a: nominal and real essence
explanation: The classical idea of definition has led to philosophers' distinction between nominal and real essence.

question_text: According to the course material, a stipulative definition is one that a term whether new or existing is given a new meaning:
option_a: for the purpose of argument or discussion in a given context
explanation: A stipulative definition therefore is one that a term whether new or existing is given a new meaning for the purpose of argument or discussion in a given context (Uduma: 2015).

question_text: According to Layman (2000), cited in the course material, until the year 2000 the word double-dodge had:
option_a: no generally accepted meaning
explanation: Until the year 2000, the word double-dodge had no generally accepted meaning.

question_text: According to the course material, double-dodge means the anticipatory movements people commonly make when they nearly collide and are trying to:
option_a: avoid such collision
explanation: Double-dodge means the anticipatory movements people commonly make when they nearly collide with some person and are trying to avoid such collision (Layman, 2000: 98).

question_text: According to the course material, some terms cannot be defined, e.g. generalissima, unity, because:
option_a: we cannot assign any higher genus under which they may fall
explanation: There are some terms that cannot be defined, e.g. generalissima, unity, and so on. This is because we cannot assign any higher genus under which they may fall.

question_text: According to the course material, Wittgenstein rejected the idea that:
option_a: every explanation of the meaning of a term needed itself to be explained
explanation: Wittgenstein rejected the very idea that every explanation of the meaning of a term needed itself to be explained. To him, there is no need to support an explanation with another explanation.

question_text: According to the course material, John Locke concludes that we cannot define individuals because:
option_a: names are learned by connecting an idea with sound, so speaker and hearer have the same idea when the word is used
explanation: John Locke on the other hand simply conclude that we cannot define individuals. This is because names are learned by connecting an idea with sound, so that speaker and hearer have the same idea when the word is used.

question_text: According to the course material, the two pairs of categorical propositions derive their names from the Latin words:
option_a: Affirmo and Nego
explanation: The two pairs derive their names from the Latin words Affirmo and Nego which stand for affirmative and negative, respectively.

question_text: According to the course material, under Affirmo we have:
option_a: universal affirmative and particular affirmative
explanation: Under Affirmo we have universal affirmative and particular affirmative while in Nego we have Universal Negative and Particular Negative.

question_text: According to the course material, in shorthand, A is for universal affirmative: All S is P; E is for Universal Negative: No S is P; I is for particular affirmative: Some S is P; O is for:
option_a: particular Negative: Some S is not P
explanation: A is for universal affirmative: All S is P. E is for Universal Negative: No S is P. I is for particular affirmative: Some S is P. O is for particular Negative: Some S is not P.

question_text: According to the course material, in its standard form, a categorical proposition is:
option_a: quantity/subject, class/quality, copula/predicate class
explanation: In its standard form, a categorical proposition is as follows: quantity/subject, class/quality, copula/predicate class.
